```{r}
#| label: load-results
#| include: false

source("report-helpers.R")
input_dir <- file.path(report_project_root(), "manuscript", "generated", "prior-sensitivity")
files <- c("candidates.csv", "diagnostics.csv", "support.csv", "contrasts.csv", "headline-contrast.png")
if (!all(file.exists(file.path(input_dir, files)))) {
  stop("Generate the prior-sensitivity reporting files using sensitivity/run_prior_sensitivity.R.")
}
read_result <- function(name) {
  readr::read_csv(file.path(input_dir, paste0(name, ".csv")), show_col_types = FALSE)
}
candidates <- read_result("candidates")
diagnostics <- read_result("diagnostics")
support <- read_result("support")
contrasts <- read_result("contrasts")
outcomes <- c(whole_body = "Whole-body lean/fat-free mass",
              hypertrophy = "Muscle size or mass", strength = "Strength",
              `function` = "Physical function")
expected <- expand.grid(outcome = names(outcomes), model_index = 1:26)
ids <- function(x) paste(x$outcome, x$model_index)
if (nrow(candidates) != nrow(expected) ||
    !setequal(ids(candidates), ids(expected)) ||
    nrow(diagnostics) != 5L * nrow(expected) ||
    !setequal(ids(diagnostics), ids(expected)) ||
    anyDuplicated(diagnostics[c("outcome", "model_index", "prior", "power")])) {
  stop("Run sensitivity/run_prior_sensitivity.R to generate the full 104-candidate results.")
}
outcome_order <- function(x) factor(outcomes[x], levels = unname(outcomes))
prior_label <- function(x) {
  unname(c(joint = "Saved prior terms", empirical = "Empirical intercept and RT priors")[x])
}
pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x)
assessed <- diagnostics[diagnostics$prior != "baseline", ]
valid <- is.finite(contrasts$mean_change)
reliable_contrasts <- contrasts[valid, ]
headline <- subset(reliable_contrasts, current == 0.8 & proposed == 1.6)
changed <- subset(reliable_contrasts, conclusion_changed)
equivalence_changes <- with(changed, sum(conclusion == "equivalence" |
                                         conclusion_baseline == "equivalence"))
gain_changes <- with(changed, sum(conclusion == "gain" | conclusion_baseline == "gain"))
strength_example <- subset(reliable_contrasts,
  outcome == "strength" & model_index == 4 & rt == "RT" &
    current == 0.8 & proposed == 1.6 & prior == "joint" & power == 1.2)
max_change <- function(x) {
  if (all(is.na(x))) "—" else sprintf("%.1f", 100 * max(abs(x), na.rm = TRUE))
}
```

## Methods

This exploratory check used archived posterior draws from all 104 accepted
candidates in the updated primary relative-intake analysis, with 26 candidates
for each of four outcomes. It included candidates that constrain the dose
contrast to zero and candidates with targeted prior remedies described in the
[preregistration deviations](preregistration-deviations.html). Each candidate
was evaluated separately. The original stacking weights are shown for context.

We used the prior power-scaling method of @kallioinenDetectingDiagnosingPrior2024
with powers 0.8 and 1.2. Within each fit, we multiplied the original draw
weights by the selected prior density raised to the power minus one, then
smoothed and normalised those weights using Pareto-smoothed importance sampling.
The first set of comparisons scaled all prior terms accumulated in the saved
Stan `lprior` variable, which includes the explicit coefficient and variance
priors. Standard-normal latent effects specified separately in the Stan model
block retained their original distributions. The second set scaled only the
empirically derived Student-$t$ priors on the intercept and resistance-training
(RT) coefficient. The original posterior corresponds to uniform reweighting.

We compared doses within a common age and follow-up profile. The primary models use additive effects for these covariates, so the original 25-year/12-week and the reported median profiles produce the same within-draw dose differences. We assessed
seven positive increments, including 0.8 to 1.6, 0.8 to 2.4, and 1.6 to
2.4 g/kg/day. Both endpoints had to lie within the observed intake range for
the outcome and RT condition. For each comparison, we computed the weighted
mean, equal-tailed 95% credible interval, and probabilities of meaningful
gain (above 0.10), practical equivalence (within ±0.10), and meaningful
loss (below −0.10), in standardised units. We applied the manuscript's 95%
probability criterion to classify each contrast. We report reweighted
estimates when Pareto-$k$ is below $\min(0.7, 1 - 1/\log_{10}(S))$, where
$S$ is the number of draws, and the estimated importance-sampling effective
sample size is at least 400.

## Prior sensitivity of the dose contrasts

`r sum(assessed$reliable)` of `r nrow(assessed)` candidate and perturbation
combinations met both importance-sampling criteria. There were
`r sum(!support$supported)` candidate and RT-specific dose pairs outside the
observed intake range. Among the `r sum(valid)` reliable reweighted contrast
comparisons, `r sum(contrasts$conclusion_changed, na.rm = TRUE)` crossed a
95% decision threshold relative to their original candidate fit.

```{r}
#| label: fig-prior-headline
#| fig-cap: "Change in the posterior mean contrast for raising intake from 0.8 to 1.6 g/kg/day. Each point is a candidate with reliable reweighting and both doses in the observed range. Vertical jitter separates overlapping points within each row. The dashed line marks zero change from the original fit."
#| fig-alt: "Shifts in candidate posterior means for the 0.8 to 1.6 gram per kilogram per day contrast, by outcome, resistance training condition, and prior perturbation."
#| out-width: "100%"

knitr::include_graphics(file.path(input_dir, "headline-contrast.png"))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-prior-probability-changes
#| tbl-cap: "Largest absolute change from each original fit in posterior means (standardised units) and probabilities (percentage points). Counts cover candidate, dose pair, and perturbation combinations. A dash indicates no reliable comparison."

summary <- contrasts |>
  dplyr::mutate(outcome = outcome_order(outcome)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(outcome, rt, prior) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    reliable = sum(!is.na(mean_change)),
    total = dplyr::n(),
    mean_shift = if (all(is.na(mean_change))) "—" else
      sprintf("%.4f", max(abs(mean_change), na.rm = TRUE)),
    gain = max_change(gain_change),
    equivalence = max_change(equivalence_change),
    loss = max_change(loss_change),
    changed = sum(conclusion_changed, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Outcome = summary$outcome,
  RT = summary$rt,
  `Prior terms` = prior_label(summary$prior),
  `Reliable / eligible` = paste(summary$reliable, summary$total, sep = " / "),
  `Mean shift` = summary$mean_shift,
  Gain = summary$gain,
  Equivalence = summary$equivalence,
  Loss = summary$loss,
  `Classification changes` = ifelse(summary$reliable > 0, summary$changed, "—"),
  check.names = FALSE
))
```

## Overall interpretation

The tested prior changes had little effect on the magnitude of the
candidate-level dose contrasts. The largest absolute shift in a posterior
mean was `r sprintf("%.3f", max(abs(reliable_contrasts$mean_change)))`
standardised units across all comparisons and
`r sprintf("%.3f", max(abs(headline$mean_change)))` for the 0.8 to 1.6 g/kg/day
comparison, relative to a smallest effect size of interest of ±0.10.
When only the empirical intercept and RT priors were perturbed, the largest
mean shift was
`r sprintf("%.3f", max(abs(reliable_contrasts$mean_change[reliable_contrasts$prior == "empirical"])))`
standardised units.

At the 95% probability threshold,
`r nrow(changed)` of `r format(nrow(reliable_contrasts), big.mark = ",")`
comparisons (`r pct(nrow(changed) / nrow(reliable_contrasts))`) changed
classification. Of these, `r equivalence_changes` moved between practical
equivalence and uncertainty, and `r gain_changes` moved between meaningful
gain and uncertainty. Posterior probabilities could shift even when the
classification held. For example, for strength model 4 with RT, jointly
scaling the saved prior terms to 1.2 reduced the probability of a meaningful
gain from 0.8 to 1.6 g/kg/day from `r pct(strength_example$gain_baseline)`
to `r pct(strength_example$gain)`. The contrast remained uncertain.

The results support local robustness of the candidate-level contrast
estimates to the prior changes tested. Decisions close to the 95% threshold
can still depend on prior strength. This analysis evaluated model candidates
separately. Assessing the sensitivity of the model-averaged results would
require updating the leave-one-out predictions and stacking weights under
the perturbed priors.
